### Game of life rules:

For a cell to live in the next iteration, it needs to have 2 or 3 neighboring cells that are alive. If it has more than 3, it dies due to overpopulation. If it has fewer than 2, it dies due to underpopulation.

For a cell to be born in the next iteration, it needs to have exactly 3 neighboring cells that are alive.

The grid is considered to wrap around in both directions. So, for example, the cells on the right edge are considered to be neighbors of the cells on the left edge, and the cells on the top edge are considered to be neighbors of the cells on the bottom edge.
